steps: Speed is the distance covered by an object in unit time.
Velocity is the displacement of an object in unit time in a specified direction.
Speed is a scalar quantity; it has magnitude only.
Velocity is a vector quantity; it has both magnitude and direction.
items.finalAnswer: Speed is distance per unit time and a scalar; velocity is displacement per unit time in a specified direction and a vector.

steps: Translatory motion: A body moves from one place to another, and all its points move the same distance in the same direction. It may be linear, circular or random.
Example: A car moving along a straight road has linear motion; a stone tied to a string and whirled has circular motion; the motion of a flying insect is random motion.
Rotatory motion: A body spins about an axis passing through it.
Example: The motion of a ceiling fan or a wheel about its axle.
Vibratory motion: A body moves to and fro about its mean position.
Example: The motion of a simple pendulum or a vibrating tuning fork.
items.finalAnswer: The three types of motion are translatory, rotatory and vibratory motion.

steps: Distance is the length of the actual path covered by a moving body.
Displacement is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions of a body in a specified direction.
Distance is a scalar quantity, whereas displacement is a vector quantity.
Distance is always positive, while displacement may be positive, negative or zero.
The magnitude of displacement is always less than or equal to the distance travelled.
items.finalAnswer: Distance is the actual path length; displacement is the shortest directed distance from the initial to the final position.

items.figure: Draw two separate graphs. (1) Distance-time graph: put time on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis; draw a straight rising line and mark its gradient as Δdistance/Δtime = speed. (2) Speed-time graph: put time on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis; draw a rising straight line and mark its gradient as Δspeed/Δtime = acceleration.
steps: The gradient of a graph is the change in the quantity on the vertical axis divided by the change in the quantity on the horizontal axis.
For a distance-time graph, gradient = change in distance / change in time = speed.
For a speed-time graph, gradient = change in speed / change in time = acceleration.
Draw and label the two graphs as described in the figure.
items.finalAnswer: The gradient of a distance-time graph represents speed, and the gradient of a speed-time graph represents acceleration.

steps: Consider an object moving with uniform speed v for time t.
Distance covered, s = speed × time = vt.
The area under its speed-time graph is the area of a rectangle.
Area = base × height = t × v = vt.
Therefore, the area under the speed-time graph is equal to the distance covered. For a changing speed, the area under the graph gives the total distance covered.
items.finalAnswer: The area under a speed-time graph represents the distance covered by the object.

steps: For a body moving under gravity, the acceleration a in the equations of motion is replaced by the acceleration due to gravity g.
The equations of motion become: v = u + gt; s = ut + ½gt²; v² = u² + 2gs.
These equations apply when downward is taken as the positive direction.
If upward is taken as positive, the acceleration is −g, so g is replaced by −g in the equations.
items.finalAnswer: For motion under gravity, use the equations of motion with a = g (or a = −g when upward is positive).

items.figure: Draw x- and y-axes with their origin O. From O, draw an arrow in the first quadrant, making an angle of 60° anticlockwise from the positive x-axis. Label the arrow v = 400 m s⁻¹ and mark the 60° angle from the positive x-axis.
steps: Draw the x- and y-axes and mark their origin O.
From O, draw an arrow 60° above the positive x-axis.
Put the arrowhead at the end of the line and label it v = 400 m s⁻¹.
items.finalAnswer: A velocity vector of 400 m s⁻¹ directed at 60° to the positive x-axis.

steps: Draw the x- and y-axes and mark their origin O.
From O, draw an arrow 120° anticlockwise from the positive x-axis; the arrow lies in the second quadrant.
Put the arrowhead at the end of the line and label it F = 50 N.
items.finalAnswer: A force vector of 50 N directed at 120° to the positive x-axis.
